doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Singing, dancing and Sun Ra's expressions
summary: Sun Ra wanted musicians to sing, dance and entertain, not sit stiffly; Allen discusses his stern look.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you guys kind of take it in stride when he instructed you to start singing?

Well now you’re a musician, you’re supposed to be able to carry a tune and you’re playing one, and you’ll be able to not sit there like a musician all straight up and stiff and playing correct, because life ain’t like that no way. So that’s why he left some space in there where you could be what it is. You write a form, and the space in between you put it in. See?
I hear that you just finished —

So then you have to dance, sing, and be a clown and everything else. You’ve got to be a natural person who does things in your life. You know. So that’s why I say most of the musicians would sit down and play their horn and wipe their mouth and sit there like that. But no, that’s not entertaining. You put on some colors, people are looking and feel it, and when you’re playing they see all these nice clothes and the [inaudible] people. And you’re not just sitting there like a statue. You’re dancing like they would dance, you’re singing, you’re doing all these things. So that’s what he wanted the musicians to do besides playing the music.
The things that I’ve seen, the pictures, the video and the photographs, it seemed to me, and I very well could be wrong, but that Sun Ra usually had the same expression on his face.
Well his expressions were — his expressions, they were like the same expression on my face. I laugh [gestures] it’s nothing.
You know I mean but you know if he gets into a certain look then you say uh oh, what did I do.
Then you see an expression, huh?
Yeah. But when you do something you’d get that look then you go uh oh, what have I done now, you see?
